content_metadata.description: An insightful interview with Swami Nikhilanand, hosted by RJ Gomathy, exploring spiritual themes such as Karma and Roopa Dhyan.

qAndA.answer: He holds up a small, white, round object.
qAndA.question: What is the visual element Swami Nikhilanand uses to represent the concept of Karma?

qAndA.answer: It helps to focus during Dhyan (meditation) by visualizing a loved one.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of Roopa Dhyan as explained in the interview?

qAndA.answer: The mind, which he refers to as "Man."
qAndA.question: What does Swami Nikhilanand describe as the "medium" for carrying Karma?

qAndA.answer: Sanchit Karma, Prarabdha Karma, and Kriyaman Karma.
qAndA.question: What specific terminology does Swami Nikhilanand use to describe the three types of Karma?

qAndA.answer: He describes it as a cycle of traveling, teaching, meditating, studying, and administrative tasks, emphasizing his love for sharing his knowledge and connecting with people.
qAndA.question: How does Swami Nikhilanand describe his daily life?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: It was wonderful to know about the Rube Dhyan, where we are talking about the form,
whoever we love, if we can bring them in, it is easier to focus, like getting some focus
helps a lot for doing Dhyan. So, I was like really impressed with the Rube Dhyan.
I have another question for you, which is more about karma. We talk about karma in terms of
in a day to day life. We do actions and in turn we accumulate more and more good karma as well as
bad karma. So, we have many genmas in the past. How do we bring all those along with us?
What is the medium for it to carry over?
Oh, good question. So, actually when the soul leaves the body, it doesn't go alone.
The mind also goes with the soul. So, when we talk about our self, it is actually made
up of three parts. The Atma, Sharir, plus Mun. Mun or the mind is an extremely subtle,
maïk energy. It is a material energy, whereas soul is actually divine. Soul is anche of Bhagwan,
it is getting a little technical, but soul is anche of Bhagwan. Mun is a part of Maya.
It is a material energy, but the two stay together. They are always together.
So, your mind doesn't change from life to life. You have the same mind in every life.
And every karma you do actually creates an impression. We call a sunscar in the mind.
A very subtle impression that the mind retains that impression, which has the quality of the thought.
Karma really means thoughts. A karma is maybe expressed physically, but the force behind it is the thought.
It may be expressed verbally, but the force behind it is the thought.
So, that thought creates the impression. The quality of the thought is what determines the quality of the sunscar
and the quality of the karma, good, bad, neutral, devotional. And the intensity of it also matters.
So, you could have a very good action, a moderately good action, a mildly good action, same with bad actions.
So, all of that is just naturally impressed or recorded in the mind.
And since the mind is, you could say the levels of subtlety in the mind go on and on and on and on.
So, when the medium in which you are recording it is so subtle, you can basically record an infinite amount of information in the mind.
Which is good. Since we have lived unlimited lifetimes, every soul being eternal, we have unlimited past karma, all recorded in our mind.
It is called San Chit Karma. The karma we are performing in this life is called Kriyamon Karma.
And all of our previous lives karma is also stored, like you can say on a hard disk or a hard drive.
Deep in our unconscious mind, that San Chit Karma is stored and it goes with us from life to life.
It is also, if you want a different model to think of it, we have a Katern Sharir.
So, that Katern Sharir is actually that all those sunscars, that becomes the Katern or the cause of our next incarnation.
And also, part of that San Chit Karma is given to us as our Pradabh, which is the destiny we have to undergo in this particular life.
There is still a lot of more San Chit Karma there, but we are given a part of that to Bhog.
And we have to undergo the good and bad consequences in this life.
And simultaneously we are performing Nukar.
So, one shouldn't think that because I have a destiny, everything is destined.
Certain things are destined, like the birth we are given, the family we are born into.
Certain things that happen to us that are out of our control, we call good luck or bad luck, that is all destined.
But our thoughts, our actions, our words, our reactions to situations, our decisions, those are not destined.
And that is how we create the new Karma, which becomes our destiny for our next life.
So, we always have that San Chit Pradabh and Kriyamon Karma, the three of them are always with us.
Very nice. It is very interesting to know about the different things that we are not aware of in our whole life.
So, it is interesting to know about those to be aware of it, so that we, whatever actions we do, we have to be conscious about what we are doing.
Yes. So, on a day to day life, how is your day looks like? What did you do?
My day as a, my role actually in serving my Guruji is to be a pracharak to go around and teach others about what I learned.
So, it is a great blessing for me to get the chance to share it because this knowledge made such a difference in my life.
And I love to teach anyway, so to get the chance to share it with others.
And thereby also continuously review it myself and keep it fresh in my mind. It is a big blessing.
So, as a part of that, I travel almost constantly from city to city around the United States and give lectures in Hindu temples mostly.
Sometimes in other venues and lot in people's homes as well. And I stay in, pretty much stay in a different home every night.

So, that is part of my role as well as to stay with people and give them a chance to ask questions and maybe hopefully inspire them on their spiritual path, teach them ways that they can integrate spirituality into their daily life.
So, part of my day is spending time with people. Normally in the evenings I have a lecture or a meditation program.
Early in the morning I like to get up and do my own meditation. I get up and do Rupthyaan.
Listen to Kirtthen and do Rupthyaan. Same thing before I go to sleep at night.
I exercise every day because keeping the body healthy is essential for keeping the mind healthy. So, I do some yoga, walking, jogging, some kind of exercise every day.
And part of my day is studying, part of my day is administrative things, setting up future programs. That is generally how my life goes.
And then I take breaks. I go to India probably twice a year to take part in meditation intensives in our osherums over there. So, those are the things I really look forward to.
A lot of work. It is what I wanted to do. So, I don't see it as well.
That is a good thing. So, what brought you here to Dallas?
Here in Dallas we actually have an affiliated center of Radham Adavdham. Radham Adavdham is the main US center of Jagatguru Kripalu Parishat, my Guruji's organization.
So, although the main center is in Austin, we have affiliated centers throughout the US. And one of those is here in Dallas in Irving. It is called Radha Guvinda Dham.
So, I am actually speaking here this whole week, giving a series of lectures on the Lila's of Shri Krishna described as described in the Bhagwat, the Shri Mat Bhagwat Purana.
So, if anyone wants to come out they can come and join us at the Mandir.
Yeah, that is interesting. Radha Guvinda Dham in Irving, Texas.
That is right. It is in the MacArthur area, right?
That is right.
And you can just google Radha Guvinda Dham Dallas and you will find us.
So, I heard that you have a beautiful voice. So, can you just sing us a small kirtan?
I can sing a couple lines of a Bhajan composed by my Guruji, a simple Radha Guvinda.

Swami Nikhilanand interviewed at Desiplaza Studio in Irving on January 25th, 2017.

Swami Nikhilanand is a prominent, Canadian born Hindu Spiritual Leader. He is the spiritual teacher at Radha Madhav Dham, One of the largest Hindu Temple complexes in the Western Hemisphere and the largest in North America.

A sanyasi and disciple of Jagadguruttam Kripalu Maharaj, and a teacher of the worldwide organization Jagadguru Kripalu Parishat with his spiritual teacher's blessings, Swami Nikhilanand regularly delivers speeches, workshops and large family camps throughout the United States. The main aim of his organization, JKP Radha Madhav Dham, is to teach the knowledge of the Hindu scriptures and to teach the practical devotion to God.
